In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FC+ cows have a lower milk yield compared with FC- cows, but that the reduction is not as high as expected from other studies.
the milk yield reduction of individual cows infected with MAP is influenced by the WHP and the farm effect, and that the magnitude of this reduction is not negligible.
the reduction of milk yield per infected cow depends on the within-herds prevalence of MAP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a decrease in milk production in MAP-positive cows is dependent on within-herds prevalence and farm.
a decrease in WHP is accompanied by a reduction in the number of infected cows and also by an improvement of milk yield per infected cow.

the reduction of the within- herds prevalence of paratuberculosis in a dairy herd would not only lead to a reduced number of infected animals in the herd but also to a reduced individual loss in milk production per animal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a decrease of the WHP is not only associated with the reduction in the number of infected individuals, but also with a decrease in the individual loss of milk production per infected individual.
the decrease in milk production in cows infected with paratuberculosis is dependent on the prevalence of paratuberculosis within the herd.

the reduction in test-day milk yield of MAP-infected cows compared with MAP-negative herd-mates is not only influenced by parity and stage of lactations, but is significantly influenced by the farm effect.
